newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Press Digest - Ireland - January 20.
newsitem.headline: Press Digest - Ireland - January 20.

text.p: Following are the highlights of stories reported in the Irish press on Monday.
- The Irish government has taken formal advise on the timing of a general election, a constitutional referendum and a possible presidential election later this year.

- The Catholic Primate, Archbishop Sean Brady, has been criticised by unionist politicians for suggesting that the British and Irish governments and the Northern parliament should accept that another "unequivocally declared" IRA ceasefire is genuine.
- The first round table talks in more than a year between the groups involved in the internal police representative dispute are expected to take place before the end of January.

- Under the Partnership 2000 agreement the Irish government is to provide 100 million Irish pounds over the next three years for a business tax package which will include reductions in corporation tax.
- Finance minister Ruairi Quinn, who will deliver his third budget on Wednesday, threatened to walk away from his post just five weeks ago.
- The leader of one of the country's largest trade unions on Sunday night called for rejection of the new national wage agreement, Partnership 2000.
- A new EU audit report on Sunday night heavily criticised the Irish government's handling of the multi-million pound Brussels beef support regime.
- The government is to offer financial assistance to Egypt to upgrade its beef slaughtering facilities in order to lessen BSE risk fears.

- ESAT Digifone, the company which holds the country's second mobile phone licence, has denied reports it has warned the Irish government that it faces collapse unless it gets special planning treatment for the erection of radio masts around the country.
